newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland's Lisheen mine gets environmental licence.
newsitem.headline: Ireland's Lisheen mine gets environmental licence.

text.p: Ivernia West Plc and Minorco Lisheen Ltd said on Tuesday that they had been granted an integrated pollution control (IPC) licence by the Environmental Protection Agency for the Lisheen zinc development in which they are partners.

"Lisheen is the first mine project in Ireland to be granted an IPC licence by the EPA and the licence will ensure that the Lisheen mine will operate in accordance with some of the strictest environmental and safety conditions anywhere in the world," Ivernia said in a statement.
The licence sets stringent standards for air and water quality, noise levels and waste disposal practices at the mine.

The Lisheen project was given final planning permission in May and discussions are continuing with Ireland's Department of the Marine and Natural Resources to finalise arrangements for the granting of a state mining lease.

Construction work, which will take nearly two years, is due to start within weeks while commercial production of zinc and lead concentrate for export to smelter in Europe and the U.S. is expected to begin in the first half of 1999, Ivernia said.
